## Interpretation

**Background.** The context-generalization line builds predictors on context activations at the assistant-header newline and measures transfer between context pairs, but had never produced a descriptive map of the representation space those predictors live in. This run is that map: no training, no outcome variable — just the joint geometry of a 50-instance context battery across all 28 layers, with a falsifiable core (family structure vs permutation null) and pre-registered length controls.

**Claim 1 (H1 — confirmed, decisively).** Under the Betley-genre probe pool, the 48 headline contexts organize by family in Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct's residual stream far above chance: max k-NN purity 0.979 (null95 0.375) and max silhouette 0.400 (null95 −0.116), each p = 0.001 after the max-over-layers FWER correction, N=48. Both co-primaries pass individually, so the result is not metric-discordant. The structure exceeds the length-only baseline (0.396) and the TF-IDF text-similarity baseline (0.604): the activation geometry contains family organization beyond what surface text statistics alone predict.

**Claim 2 (H2 — partially as predicted, with a sharper picture).** The depth profile peaks mid-network (purity L14, silhouette L18, CKA regime change at ~L13–15), consistent with the predicted mid-to-late band — but family structure is above null at EVERY layer, including layer 0 (purity 0.708 vs null95 0.292). Families differ in surface form, and that is visible to the read position from the first block; what the mid-network adds is compactness (silhouette nearly triples, 0.117 → 0.400). Late layers (L19–27) partially reorganize: pooled metrics decline modestly, the top PC decouples from length, and split-half reliability dips (0.87–0.91).

**Claim 3 (H3 — confirmed; structure is not a length artifact).** The length-residualized read still beats its null at p = 0.001 (purity 0.958 at L10), the length-only baseline explains little of the headline (0.396 of the way from chance 0.292 to observed 0.979), and same-style ICL instances cluster across a 4× length spread. Length IS a real, family-collinear axis (PC1 |Spearman| up to 0.95 vs log-length in early/mid layers; the length-only baseline itself beats chance at p = 0.005) — worth remembering when building predictors on these vectors — but it does not carry the family structure.

**Claim 4 (exploratory, the most interesting new lead — behavior instructions are absorbed into the persona region at depth).** Behavior-commanding prompts ("You refuse every request.", "You are sycophantic.", …) form a coherent family through the early/mid stack (purity up to 1.0 at L11) and then dissolve: purity 0.2 by L20 and 0.0 at L27, silhouette negative from L17, with deep-layer nearest neighbors landing among persona prompts and the helpful-assistant default. ## Interpretation

**Background.** The context-generalization line builds predictors on context activations at the assistant-header newline and measures transfer between context pairs, but had never produced a descriptive map of the representation space those predictors live in. This run is that map: no training, no outcome variable — just the joint geometry of a 50-instance context battery across all 28 layers, with a falsifiable core (family structure vs permutation null) and pre-registered length controls.

**Claim 1 (confirmed, decisively — scoped).** Under the Betley-genre probe pool, the 48 headline contexts AS CONSTRUCTED organize by family in Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct's residual stream far above chance: max k-NN purity 0.979 (null95 0.375) and max silhouette 0.400 (null95 −0.116), each p = 0.001 after the max-over-layers FWER correction, N=48. Both co-primaries pass individually, so the result is not metric-discordant. The structure exceeds the length-only baseline (purity 0.396) and the lexical (TF-IDF) text-similarity baseline (purity 0.604): the activation geometry contains family organization beyond what context length or lexical overlap alone predict. (The TF-IDF comparison is a robustness check against one surface measure; a semantic text-similarity baseline was not run.)

**Claim 2 (partially as predicted, with a sharper picture).** The depth profile peaks mid-network (purity L14, silhouette L18, CKA regime change at ~L13–15), consistent with the predicted mid-to-late band — but pooled family structure is above null at EVERY layer, including layer 0 (purity 0.708 vs null95 0.292). The L0 separability is family-specific, not universal: persona, format, and ICL contexts are separable from the first block (their surface forms differ strongly), while the rephrase family — same instruction, different registers — is at chance until L13. What the mid-network adds is compactness (pooled silhouette nearly triples, 0.117 → 0.400) and the late convergence of the rephrase family. Late layers (L19–27) partially reorganize: pooled metrics decline modestly, behavior dissolves (Claim 4), WildChat's global compactness drops to ≈0 silhouette at L19–21 while its purity holds at 0.8, the top PC decouples from length, and split-half reliability dips (0.87–0.91).

**Claim 3 (confirmed; structure is not a length artifact).** The length-residualized read still beats its null at p = 0.001 (purity 0.958 at L10), the length-only baseline reaches purity 0.396 — real (p = 0.005 against its own null) but far below the activation read of 0.979 — and same-style ICL instances cluster across a 4× length spread. Length IS a real, family-collinear axis (PC1 |Spearman| up to 0.95 vs log-length in early/mid layers) — worth remembering when building predictors on these vectors — but it does not carry the family structure.

**Claim 4 (exploratory, the most interesting new lead — most non-marker behavior instructions drift into the persona/default region at depth).** Behavior-commanding prompts ("You refuse every request.", "You are sycophantic.", …) form a coherent family through the early/mid stack (purity 0.6–1.0 through L1–L15, max 1.0 at L11) and then disperse: purity 0.2 by L20 and 0.0 at L27, silhouette negative from L17. At L27, three of five behavior instances' nearest neighbors land among persona prompts and the helpful-assistant default — the same connected neighborhood where both bare defaults live at every depth — while two exceptions remain (the marker instance neighbors rephrase instances; the harmful instance's top neighbor is still the refusal instance). Direct relevance to `q:ctx-behavior`: at the depths where prior work found behavioral predictive signal (deep band, L25 in the cosine→EM line), most behavior instructions are NOT geometrically distinct from personas at this read position. The descriptive statement is "most non-marker behavior vectors move toward persona/default neighborhoods at late layers" — any mechanistic gloss (e.g. the model folding behavior into identity) is underdetermined by n=5 with no behavioral readout. Strictly exploratory: n=5 with k=4 makes the purity metric fragile by construction, one probe pool, lowest split-half reliability band; the proposed expanded behavior panel (15–20 instances with per-behavior paraphrases) is what would separate a real representational regularity from metric fragility plus instance idiosyncrasy. Its mirror image — the rephrase family converging from chance to the run's tightest cluster at exactly the same depths — is the complementary exploratory observation (n=6, same single-instruction caveat).

**Claim 5 (battery sanity for the testbed — passes, with named outliers).** Every family is internally coherent somewhere in the stack; the persona family coheres across disjoint house/PersonaHub templates (cross-template cosine 0.521 vs cross-family −0.165), so it is not a boilerplate artifact; within-ICL structure tracks demo style, not demo count; the bare-default anchors are now placed (persona region, all depths). **Measurement-validity note.** The Goal IS about representations, so the probing read is the construct, not a proxy for behavior; no behavioral claim is made anywhere above.
